newsitem.title: CANADA: Westar shares extend rise on sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Westar shares extend rise on sale plan.

text.p: Westar Group Ltd stock shot up Friday, extending a recent advance, on expectations that the company's plan to sell its coal port near Vancouver will bring it a big cash windfall, analysts said.
Westar stock, which has risen from around 30 in October, was up 6 to 61 in Toronto trading.

Westar announced in early December it planned a public offering of its Westshore Terminals and Moss, Lawson analyst Ivar Liepins said the sale is likely to yield C$600 million to C$700 million in two installments or C$72 to C$77 a share. This would be more than offset by tax-loss carryforwards.
"The bottom line is that when this deal goes through...Westar will be sitting with a big cash horde in excess of its current market value," Liepins said.

Westar, which is 80 percent owned by Vancouver financier Jim Pattison, has come back from near bankruptcy two years ago. Under the proposed deal it would retain a contract to manage the Westshore Terminals coal port for Westshore Terminals Income Fund, the new entity being created.
The deal is due to be voted on by Westar shareholders at a meeting January 27. Company officials were not immediately available for further comment.
